```json
{
  "winner": "A",
  "reasons": [
    "Payer and sales cycle fit the 90-day window. A sells to individual operators and consultants who can expense or self-fund a $49–$299/mo or $60-per-blueprint tool with no procurement. B's best-paying segment, banks, needs a 6–18 month cycle and SOC 2 Type II before outbound. Its reachable segment is small self-serve platforms.",
    "Willingness to pay is better anchored in A. Five competitors publish prices, and four sit at $49–$299/mo, which signals individuals pay for this category. B's self-serve competitors also publish prices, but useHUMA offers a free tier of 1,000 verifications/mo and not.bot starts at $9.99. The brief says this pushes self-serve pricing toward zero.",
    "B carries regulatory risk that A does not. The brief cites biometric-privacy exposure: BIPA and the $650M Facebook settlement, plus bans or investigations of Worldcoin in Spain, Thailand and Colombia. That is a serious liability for a solo founder to take on in a first bet.",
    "Both look buildable by one person with agents. A's pipeline is shown buildable by small teams (Foray, Gixo). B depends on open-source primitives, but the credible enterprise buyers (Zoom, banks) are already served by World ID and Incognia, or are gated by compliance.",
    "A's weaknesses are real but more survivable. The niche is dense, paid acquisition costs about $104 per lead against a $60 one-off price, and its own demand quote ('the spreadsheet can't choose between them. Only you can.') partly argues against a tool. Even so, finding one paying individual through organic channels in 90 days is more plausible than closing a platform or bank customer."
  ],
  "weakest_evidence_in_loser": "B's demand quote from Trevor Traina of Tools for Humanity ('establishing trust online becomes essential') is a competitor executive's marketing line in a partnership announcement, not evidence from a buyer. The other demand items are no closer to a payer. The r/OnlineDating quote comes from an end user who would not pay, and the $243K deepfake wire is a single anecdote republished by a bank. None shows a platform willing to buy verification from a new solo vendor.",
  "confidence_note": "Moderate confidence. A wins mainly because B's go-to-market is structurally mismatched to a 90-day solo timeline, not because A's evidence is strong. A's demand evidence is two social posts about decision paralysis, one of which undercuts the tool premise. A also has no stated differentiation from Foray or MarketGeist."
}
```
